metaTitle: Deck Building in Ontario: What to Know
metaDescription: A plain guide to hiring a deck builder in Ontario, covering guard height rules, permits, material choices and realistic cost ranges for 2026.
intro: A new deck is one of the more visible home projects, and quality shows up fast in how level the frame stays and how the railings feel underfoot. Ontario's building code sets specific rules for deck height, guard rails and footings, so the builder's familiarity with local permitting matters as much as their finish carpentry.
whatToLookFor: Experience with both pressure-treated and composite or PVC decking systems
Working knowledge of Ontario Building Code guard height and stair rules
Proper footing depth for frost protection in your municipality
A clear plan for ledger board attachment and flashing against the house
Portfolio photos of multi-level or complex builds, not just simple platforms
typicalCostNotes: Costs vary widely with size, decking material and site access, but a straightforward pressure-treated deck often lands in a lower range while composite or multi-level builds with railings, stairs and lighting can run considerably higher. Site access, existing grade and how far the crew has to move materials also affect price, so treat any early number as a rough range until a site visit happens.
questionsToAsk: Will you pull the building permit, and is my deck height over the threshold that requires one?
What footing depth and spacing are you using for this soil and frost line?
How is the ledger board flashed to prevent water getting behind the siding?
What warranty covers labour separately from the material manufacturer's warranty?
Can I see a deck you built at least two years ago to check how it has aged?
redFlags: Offers to skip the permit on a deck clearly over the height threshold
Vague or missing detail on footing depth and frost protection
No fixed schedule for deposits tied to project milestones
